---
title: "Fall-through"
---

In C, a `case` keeps running into the next one unless you write `break`, and "forgot the
`break`" is a bug old enough to have its own folklore. switchlang turns that around: a case
stops after itself unless you ask it to fall through. This page shows how to ask, and what
runs when you do.

## Opt in per case

Pass `fallthrough=True` on a case, and when that case matches, the next registered case runs
as well, whether or not its own key matches:

```{python}
from switchlang import switch


def run(value):
    log = []
    with switch(value) as s:
        s.case(1, lambda: log.append('one'))
        s.case(2, lambda: log.append('two'), fallthrough=True)
        s.case(3, lambda: log.append('three'))
        s.case(4, lambda: log.append('four'))
        s.default(lambda: log.append('other'))
    return log


print(run(1), run(2), run(3), run(9))
```

Only the `2` case asked to fall through, so only a value of `2` runs two actions. `3` runs
alone; it doesn't fall into `4`.

## Chains

A case that was fallen into can itself fall through. The chain continues until it reaches a
case without `fallthrough=True`:

```{python}
with switch('a') as s:
    s.case('a', lambda: 'a', fallthrough=True)
    s.case('b', lambda: 'b', fallthrough=True)
    s.case('c', lambda: 'c')
    s.case('d', lambda: 'd')
    s.default(lambda: 'default')

print(s.result)
```

`'a'` matched and fell through to `'b'`, which fell through to `'c'`, which stopped. The
`'d'` case never ran, and `s.result` is the return value of the last function that did.

## Falling into `default`

`default()` is just another registered case, so if the case before it falls through, the
default runs too:

```{python}
with switch('a') as s:
    s.case('a', lambda: 'a', fallthrough=True)
    s.default(lambda: 'default')

print(s.result)
```

This is also a reason to register `default()` last: it should be the end of any chain, not
the middle of one.

## With list and range keys

Fall-through on a list or range case applies when any of its items matches. A list or range
case that is fallen *into* runs once, not once per item:

```{python}
with switch(2) as s:
    s.case([1, 2], lambda: 'one or two', fallthrough=True)
    s.case(range(3, 6), lambda: 'three to five')
    s.default(lambda: 'other')

print(s.result)
```

## Results under fall-through

Every function in the chain runs, and `s.result` is the return value of the *last* one.
If you need the intermediate values, collect them yourself, as `run()` above does with its
`log` list. [Results](results.qmd) has more.

## `fallthrough=None`

The `fallthrough` parameter accepts `True` or `False`. The value `None` is reserved for
switchlang's own use while it expands list and range keys; don't pass it.
